Which records can answer which question

Source: R/crt_schema_grade.R
crt_schema_grade.Rd

Evaluates each grade a registered schema declares against every row of a data frame. A row meets a grade when every column the grade requires is present in the frame and non-missing in that row.

Usage

crt_schema_grade(df, source, file_name)

Arguments

df

A data frame, usually the output of crt_schema_conform().

source

Character. Source family code (e.g. "nge").

file_name

Character. Logical file name (e.g. "form_pscis").

Value

A tibble with one logical column per declared grade, in declaration order, and one row per row of df.

Details

A grade is a separate thing from the schema's required flag, on purpose. Columns added to a form mid-season are optional in the schema, so a record from an earlier vintage still conforms; whether that record can answer a given question is asked here. Making the new columns required would make the earlier records unharvestable, and having no grade would count them as equivalent to records that carry the extra fields.

A column the frame does not have at all fails the grade for every row: an earlier vintage that never asked the question cannot answer it.

Throws when the schema declares no grades.

See also

crt_schema_cols() for the columns themselves.

Examples

records <- data.frame(
  project = "example", form = "form_monitoring_fish_passage",
  record_id = 1:2, source_version = "v1",
  schema_version = "35-0000000000000000",
  captured_at = "2026-09-21T18:00:00Z",
  x = c(1203451, NA), y = c(1012345, 1012400), source_epsg = 3005L
)
crt_schema_grade(records, "nge", "form_monitoring_fish_passage")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   harvestable
#>   <lgl>      
#> 1 TRUE       
#> 2 FALSE
